html:
The Cypriot financial crisis came to a head in March 2013, when Cyprus agreed a bailout with the European Union and the International Monetary Fund that closed its second largest bank and took a large share of big deposits.

Cypriot banks had grown to several times the size of the economy, drawing deposits from Russia and elsewhere, and lost heavily on Greek government bonds during the European debt crisis. Banks were shut for nearly two weeks and capital controls imposed, the first in the eurozone. Laiki Bank was wound up and deposits above 100,000 euros at the Bank of Cyprus were turned into shares. The economy shrank sharply before recovering. The bail in became a model for later bank rescues in the eurozone.
sum: The Cypriot financial crisis came to a head in March 2013, when Cyprus agreed a bailout with the European Union and the International Monetary Fund that closed its second largest bank and took a large share of big deposits.
